newsitem.title: USA: First Enterprise sees Q4 below estimates.
newsitem.headline: First Enterprise sees Q4 below estimates.

text.p: First Enterprise Financial Group Inc on Thursday estimates its fourth quarter will be profitable, but below analysts' estimates.

The company, which buys and services installment sales contracts originated by automobile dealers for financing the sale of used cars, said it was reviewing its portfolio and static pool data in light of recent developments in the industry.

"We will use this opportunity to build our reserves, and to absorb previously unanticipated chargeoffs," said chairman Michael Harrington in a statement. "This is a one-time occurrence and will not affect our ongoing operations."
Company spokesmen were not immediately available for further comment.

On a preliminary basis, the company said net income per share for the quarter is estimated to be between $0.05 and $0.10 and pro forma income per share will be between $0.67 and $0.72 for the 1996 year.
The pro forma income per share in 1995 was $0.42.
